results.title: GPU Rental Prices Are Going Up. The Token Price Is Not. - Tech Thought Leaders
highlights:
Executive Summary

Rented GPU capacity is getting more expensive while the price of a token keeps falling. Nebius will raise on-demand rates for the H100, H200, B200 and B300 from 1 October, its second increase in three months, with the B300 up 21 percent to $9.50 a GPU hour. The memory tier moved further still, and Genoa memory rose about 41 percent.

...

The cheapest way to buy AI compute is not getting cheaper. From 1 October, Nebius raises the on-demand rate for four Nvidia accelerators, and it is the second rise in three months. The number most teams track, cost per token, is still heading down.

...

## The new rate card is not a rounding error

Nebius published the change on its own pricing page. The H100 moves from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, up 17 percent. The H200 rises 20 percent to $5.40. The B200 rises 19 percent to $8.50. The B300 takes the steepest step, up 21 percent to $9.50.

Add the three months since the previous change, and the B300 rate is up roughly 56 percent. The increases were not limited to accelerators. Nebius lifted the AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU rate 25 percent and the Genoa memory rate about 41 percent.

Trackers saw the pressure earlier.

...

Here is the mechanism. The newer the chip, the more high-bandwidth memory it carries, and memory has been the tightest part of the build, as memory market trackers keep recording. The Genoa memory rate rose about 41 percent in the same change, which is the memory squeeze showing up on the bill.

results.title: Nebius lifts on-demand GPU hours up to 21% | Wire
highlights:
Nebius lifts on-demand GPU hours up to 21% | Wire

# Nebius lifts on-demand GPU hours up to 21%

Nebius prices page (live 3 Oct): Oct 1 on-demand card H100 $3.85→$4.50, B300 $7.85→$9.50. A list hike is not collected cash.

#### Sean

 03 Oct 2026 — 6 min read 

`WIRE` · `NEOCLOUDS` · `GLOBAL` · Data as at 2–3 Oct 2026

Nebius’s public price page still prints two columns: the prior on-demand GPU-hour and a second column marked effective 1 October 2026. Selected Nvidia rows move 16.9% to 21.0% — H100 from $3.85 to $4.50, B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. On the neoclouds layer, a posted card is ready list. It is not settled invoice cash until customers bill and renew at the new walk-up. Ready is not paid.

## What happened

Nebius’s prices page (live-checked 3 October 2026; FinanceFeeds confirmed both columns still visible on 2 October) posts an October 1 effective card that lifts on-demand rates on the accelerators customers are queued for. RTX PRO 6000 stays $1.80. GB200 and GB300 NVL72 racks stay contact us. Commitment discounts remain up to 35% off on-demand; spot floors print from $0.79 (H100/H200) and $0.99 (B200/B300).

Event

Nebius posts Oct 1 on-demand GPU-hour card — selected Nvidia rows +16.9% to +21.0%

nebius.com/prices live-checked 3 Oct 2026; FinanceFeeds 2 Oct — both columns still printed

H100 move

$3.85 → $4.50 (+16.9%) — prior-generation Hopper still dearer to rent

8×H100 × 720h list: ~$22,176 → ~$25,920 — list math, not invoices

B300 (top of range)

$7.85 → $9.50 (+21.0%) — “up to 21%” is this row

H200 $4.50→$5.40 (+20.0%); B200 $7.15→$8.50 (+18.9%)

CoreWeave $40M/MW (separate unit)

Q3 short contracts ~3–6 months at ~$40M per MW annualized

CoreWeave IR, 17 Sep 2026 — $/MW ≠ Nebius $/GPU-hour; do not invent H100-equivalent

Stuck step named

Utilization + billing at the new walk-up (and short-book contract performance)

Posted Oct 1 card ≠ settled invoice

Do not treat the right-hand column as what every customer already pays. FinanceFeeds noted GPU Finder’s Oct 2 tracker still mixed — some GPUs on the old column, H200 already on the new. A list hike is not collected cash.

## Why cash cares

On the neoclouds layer, cash for walk-up GPU hours clears when hours are consumed and invoices clear at the rate the console bills — see Neocloud explained and Who finances GPU clusters?. A dual-column price page after the effective date is ready list talk. It is not yet paid. That gap is the whole Wire: Nebius can date the card 1 October, and still be waiting on utilization and billing when both columns sit on the same page.

Two cash clocks:

1. Card vs bill. H100 $3.85 → $4.50 and B300 $7.85 → $9.50 are posted list moves. An 8×H100 box at 720 hours goes from about $22,176 to $25,920 on list math — before tax, storage, or a commitment discount, and not an invoice. Nebius gets paid if on-demand hours clear at the new walk-up; customers on older commitments, discounts up to 35%, or spot from $0.79/$0.99 are not paying $4.50 or $9.50.
2. GPU-hour vs megawatt. CoreWeave’s 17 September IR print is short-dated contracts (~3–6 months) at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue, plus >$25 billion net new commitments early Q3 (not in the 30 June backlog) and contracted power ~ 4.2 GW as of 11 August from ~ 3.7 GW at 30 June. That is a different unit from Nebius’s GPU-hour. Do not invent an H100-equivalent hour from MW. CoreWeave gets paid if those short contracts perform; the IR does not publish a public H100 card.

...

The announced October 1 column is not yet the only column. FinanceFeeds’ Oct 2 check and the live page on Oct 3 still show the prior on-demand figures beside the new ones. GPU Finder was mixed (H200 new; H100/B200/B300 still showing old on one snapshot). Do not invent that every customer already pays $4.50 or $9.50.

results.title: 海外算力租赁价格中枢上移，Nebius涨价17%到21%，国内合同金额同步上修！_腾讯新闻
highlights:
截至 11时 09分南威软件连续 6天涨停，迈信林触及 20厘米涨停板，超讯科技、蜂助手、佳华科技等个股纷纷跟涨。盘面交易的主要变化，并不是因为概念热度的增加，而是海外GPU租赁价格出现了比较大的上调。

证券时报报道说云计算服务提供商Nebius宣布自 10月1日起对各项按需计算资源的价格进行了调整，英伟达最新一代GPU的租金涨幅最大。

价格调整之后,H 100从每GPU小时 3.85美元涨到 4.50美元，上涨了约 17%；H 200从 4.5美元涨到 5.4美元，上涨幅度为 20%；B 200从 7.15升至 8.5，涨幅接近 19%。英伟达B 30的价格由原来的 7． 86元每小时涨到了现在的 9． 5元每小时，涨幅达到了 21%，这是同一批GPU价格上调之后的最高价。在同一批GPU价格同时上涨的情况下，算力租赁行业又重新引起市场关注。

这里的按需价格是指客户临时租用算力时所面对的即时价格。“按需”一般指客户临时租用时的价格，而“price”则指的是根据客户的实际使用情况来确定的价格。浙商证券认为,Nebius本轮价格全面上调 17%到 21%，会使边际零售价体系整体上移。新签客户和中小客户通常会直接参照这种价格，因此按需价格也就成了观察行业价格中枢的一个重要锚点。

租金上涨不是利润同步增长的结果，企业仍然要面对GPU采购成本、机房建设、网络、电力和运维等各个方面的因素。但是由于海外按需价格上行，给市场提供了一个明确的价格信号，即高性能GPU的租赁价格正在发生变化，原有的报价体系也需要重新评估。

results.title: Would Falling GPU Rental Prices Rescue Frontier AI Margins? - AI Tech Model
highlights:
According to AInvest's September 2026 analysis, H100 rentals fell from over $7.00 per GPU-hour in early 2024 to a cohort median around $3.30-$3.40 by mid-2026 CoreWeave GPU rental analysis. The same analysis puts one rental index down about 23% from September 2024 to mid-2025. The IntuitionLabs 2026 pricing guide reports average H100 cloud rates around $3.11 in early 2026, with spot as low as $1.25, as Blackwell B200/B300 supply grew.

The FastGPU September 2026 survey of 28 clouds found the cheapest H100 on-demand listing at $1.79 versus $5.38 at Google Cloud. Crypto Briefing on neocloud Q2 2026 results says specialist GPU instances typically cost 60-70% less than equivalent AWS, Azure and Google Cloud offerings. AInvest market analysis in August 2026 ties this shift to supply moving from acute shortage in 2023 to functional balance in 2026.

results.title: GPU под наем: Nebius вдигна цените между 17 и 21%
highlights:
## Какво точно се промени в ценоразписа

Nebius обяви на 17 септември и въведе от 1 октомври нови цени на изчисленията си. Собствената документация на компанията съдържа раздел, в който старата и новата цена стоят една до друга, затова промяната не се налага да се реконструира отвън.

Часът на поискване за NVIDIA H100 минава от 3,85 на 4,50 долара. H200 отива от 4,50 на 5,40. B200 се вдига от 7,15 на 8,50, а B300 - от 7,85 на 9,50 долара на час, най-голямото поскъпване в таблицата. По съобщението на Reuters от 17 септември увеличението обхваща и машини само с процесор, с около 25%, както и паметта, с около 41%.

Че цените преди промяната са били точно тези, е записано и извън самата компания: конкурентен доставчик на изчисления е свалил ценовата страница на Nebius на 21 септември и е отбелязал същите стойности за H100, H200 и B200, преди новите да влязат в сила.

## GPU под наем: къде стои недостигът

В същата таблица стои подробност, която съобщенията подминават. Докато гарантираният час поскъпва, цените на прекъсваемите машини не се променят изобщо: H100 остава на 2,15 долара, H200 на 2,45, B200 на 3,95 и B300 на 4,30 долара на час. Прекъсваема машина е тази, която доставчикът може да отнеме, когато капацитетът потрябва другаде.

Разликата между двете колони е цената на обещанието, че машината ще бъде там. При H100 тя беше 1,70 долара на час (3,85 срещу 2,15), а сега е 2,35 (4,50 срещу 2,15). Тоест поскъпва не силиконът, а гаранцията за достъп до него.

Третата подробност е към кого е насочено. Поскъпва плащането на поискване, а не вече подписаните дългосрочни договори. Reuters отбелязва, че клиентите, които запазват големи групи машини за няколко месеца напред, получават отстъпка срещу ангажимента. Това е второто поскъпване за три месеца.

results.title: H100 Rates Fell, B200 Rates Rose 79%: The Great GPU Price Divergence of 2026 — CheapestGPU
highlights:
A September 25, 2026 SemiAnalysis report puts a number on one of the clearest GPU cloud price trends of 2026: B200 on-demand rental rates climbed 79% over three months to roughly $8.01/GPU-hr, while the H100 rental price slid to $2.65-3.38/GPU-hr over the same window. Compute-adjusted, B200 is now about 21% more expensive per unit of useful compute than H100 - a full reversal from where the two generations sat in June 2026. These are third-party market figures from SemiAnalysis, not CheapestGPU's own listing prices, and they are exactly the kind of headline number that falls apart the moment you compute-adjust it.

## The data: H100 rental price vs the B200 price increase in 2026

- B200 (on-demand, per SemiAnalysis) - roughly $8.01/GPU-hr - up 79% over the prior three months
- H100 (on-demand, per SemiAnalysis) - $2.65-3.38/GPU-hr - down over the same window

Translate the two numbers and the ranking flips. In June 2026, H100 was the pricier compute-adjusted buy. Today B200 costs about 21% more per unit of useful compute than H100 - the reversal is the story, not either sticker rate on its own.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Gap Reaches 141% Between Providers | TechSignal.news
highlights:
GPU cloud pricing has diverged into two distinct markets. In late September, the median on-demand NVIDIA H100 price across 40 providers reached $3.42 per GPU-hour, up 15% year over year. But the reported gap between hyperscalers and specialist GPU clouds now reaches 58% for H100s, 81% for B200s, and 141% for H200s. A continuously running 64-GPU H100 cluster at median pricing costs approximately $1.92 million annually before storage, networking, or software.

AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud maintain price premiums through integrated networking, identity management, compliance tooling, and procurement integration. Specialist providers including Vultr, RunPod, and Vast.ai compete on raw compute price and bare-metal performance. The economics now force a workload-specific choice: hyperscalers where integration and data locality justify the premium, neoclouds for cost-sensitive batch inference and training where orchestration complexity is manageable.

B200 capacity pricing reached $5.62 per GPU-hour, up 27.6% year to date. Enterprises comparing only instance prices understate total expenditure. A 64-GPU deployment represents roughly $1.9 million per year in compute alone, making reserved or dedicated capacity economically necessary for sustained workloads.

results.title: AWS verteuert reservierte Nvidia-GPU-Kapazität
highlights:
Amazon Web Services hebt die Preise für bestimmte reservierte GPU-Kapazitäten an. Vom 7. Oktober 2026 an gelten für mehrere mit Nvidia-Beschleunigern ausgestattete EC2-Instanzfamilien höhere Sätze bei den sogenannten Capacity Blocks for ML. Betroffen sind sowohl aktuelle Blackwell-Chips als auch ältere Nvidia-A100-GPUs. Andere Preismodelle von AWS werden durch die angekündigte Änderung dagegen nicht verteuert.

AWS Capacity Blocks ermöglichen Unternehmen, Rechenkapazität mit leistungsfähigen Beschleunigern für einen festgelegten Zeitraum im Voraus zu reservieren. Das Angebot richtet sich vor allem an rechenintensive Anwendungen wie das Training und die Anpassung von KI-Modellen. Die Preise richten sich nach AWS-Angaben nach Angebot und Nachfrage und werden regelmäßig angepasst.

## Rund 15 Prozent höhere Preise ab 7. Oktober

Für die Nvidia-basierten Instanzfamilien steigt das Preisniveau nach einem Vergleich der bisherigen und der ab 7. Oktober geltenden Sätze um rund 15 Prozent. AWS selbst veröffentlicht für den Stichtag konkrete neue Preise pro Beschleuniger und Stunde.

Am oberen Ende steht die P6-B300-Familie mit Nvidia-B300-Beschleunigern. Hier beträgt der neue Satz 16,146 Dollar je Accelerator-Stunde. Für die P6-B200-Familie mit B200-Chips werden 14,208 Dollar fällig. Bei Instanzen mit Nvidia H200 liegen die neuen Preise bei 7,895 Dollar für P5en und 6,866 Dollar für P5e. Für die mit H100-GPUs ausgestattete P5-Familie nennt AWS 5,970 Dollar je Beschleuniger und Stunde.

Auch ältere Generationen werden teurer. Für P4de mit Nvidia A100 und 80 Gigabyte Grafikspeicher steigt der maßgebliche Satz von zuvor 2,214 Dollar auf 2,546 Dollar je GPU-Stunde. Bei P4d mit A100-GPUs und 40 Gigabyte Speicher geht es von 1,475 Dollar auf 1,696 Dollar. Beide Veränderungen entsprechen ebenfalls einem Plus von rund 15 Prozent.

...

Dass auch die A100-Generation einbezogen wird, ist bemerkenswert, weil Nvidia inzwischen deutlich leistungsfähigere Chipgenerationen wie H100, H200, B200 und B300 anbietet. AWS führt die A100 jedoch weiterhin für anspruchsvolle Machine-Learning-Anwendungen.

...

## On-Demand und Savings Plans bleiben unverändert

Die Preisanpassung betrifft ausdrücklich nicht sämtliche Möglichkeiten, GPU-Leistung über Amazon EC2 zu beziehen. AWS erklärt, dass andere EC2-Capacity-Block-Preise sowie Festpreismodelle wie On-Demand und Savings Plans unverändert bleiben.

Damit lässt sich die Änderung nicht als allgemeine Erhöhung der AWS GPU-Preise verstehen. Sie betrifft ein spezielles Reservierungsmodell, bei dem Kunden verfügbare Beschleunigerkapazität für einen bestimmten Zeitraum sichern. Der Preis wird bei der Buchung festgelegt und im Voraus berechnet. Nach Abschluss einer Reservierung verändert sich der vereinbarte Betrag nicht mehr.

AWS weist darauf hin, dass die Preise für Capacity Blocks von der verfügbaren Kapazität und der Nachfrage zum Zeitpunkt der Buchung abhängen. Kunden können dabei unter anderem Zeitraum, Dauer und Umfang der gewünschten Kapazität auswählen. Bereits seit Einführung des Modells werden diese Preise nicht als dauerhaft feste Tarife behandelt.
